members.name: Kanangra Walls
members.bio: Sheer sandstone cliffs in Kanangra-Boyd National Park, in the Greater Blue Mountains World Heritage Area.
members.hours: Open 24 hours (may close for poor weather or fire danger)

members.name: Jenolan Caves
members.bio: Show-cave precinct with Caves House, closed for road repairs with reopening planned for early 2027.
members.hours: Closed for Two Mile road repairs; planned reopening early 2027 (not confirmed)

members.name: Cowra Japanese Garden
members.bio: Japanese garden and cultural centre opened in 1979, designed by Ken Nakajima.

members.name: Cowra Breakout Site
members.bio: Free site of the 1944 prisoner-of-war camp where more than 350 Japanese prisoners escaped.

members.name: Age of Fishes Museum
members.bio: Fossil fish museum in Canowindra, open Thursday to Monday and daily in NSW school holidays.

members.name: Canowindra
members.bio: Town known as the Balloon Capital of Australia, with a historic centre and the Age of Fishes Museum.

members.name: Parkes Observatory
members.bio: Radio telescope with a free visitors centre, a ticketed 3D theatre and a cafe on Telescope Road.

members.name: Plane on a Stick
members.bio: Roadside plane mounted on a stick in Apex Park by the main bridge in Forbes.

members.name: Nobbys Head
members.bio: A convict-built pier leads out to Nobbys Head, a headland with views over the harbour and Stockton Beach.
members.hours: Headland grounds weekends and public holidays, 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM

members.name: Fort Scratchley
members.bio: An 1882 headland fort and museum with guided tunnel tours, whose guns first fired in anger in 1942.

members.name: Newcastle Museum
members.bio: A free museum in three historic railway workshops covering local history, BHP steelworks and hands-on science.
members.photo_file: External photos of the Newcastle Museum, April 2026 01.jpg

members.name: Bathers Way
members.bio: A 6 km coastal path from Merewether Baths to Nobbys Beach, passing ocean baths and Strzelecki Lookout.

members.name: Newcastle Ocean Baths
members.bio: Open-air ocean baths from 1922 near Newcastle Beach, with a grandstand for sunbathing.
members.hours: Daily; change rooms from 5:30 AM; closed Wednesdays for cleaning

members.name: Merewether Ocean Baths
members.bio: Merewether's 1935 ocean baths, billed as the largest complex of their kind in the southern hemisphere.
members.hours: Daily; change rooms from 5:30 AM; closed Thursdays for cleaning

members.name: Bogey Hole
members.bio: A rock ocean pool carved by convicts at the foot of King Edward Park, a place for a dip.

members.name: Newcastle Art Gallery
members.bio: A regional gallery on Laman Street with a free ground-floor permanent collection of Australian art.

members.name: Newcastle Foreshore
members.bio: Harbourside parkland on the old rail yards with a playground and, around Queens Wharf, bars and cafes.

members.name: ANZAC Walk
members.bio: A 450 m ridgeline walk from Strzelecki Lookout to Bar Beach, with steel soldier silhouettes bearing names.

members.name: Newcastle Beach
members.bio: A surf beach right beside the city centre, a short walk from the ocean baths and the harbour foreshore.

members.name: Nobbys Beach
members.bio: A city beach below Nobbys Head, flanking Macquarie Pier, one of the safer swimming beaches in Newcastle.
members.photo_file: Nobbys Beach, New South Wales, Dec 2025 02.jpg

members.name: Bar Beach
members.bio: Regarded by many as the best of Newcastle's city beaches, good for surfing and kitesurfing.

members.name: Fernleigh Track
members.bio: A 15.5 km walking and cycling path on a former railway line from Adamstown to Belmont, through bushland.

members.name: Blackbutt Reserve
members.bio: A 182 ha bushland reserve with free wildlife exhibits, over 10 km of walking trails and a flying-fox colony.
members.hours: Wildlife exhibits 10:00 AM – 4:30 PM; picnic areas 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM

members.name: Hunter Wetlands Centre
members.bio: A regenerated 45 ha wetland at Shortland with walking, cycling and canoe trails, a visitor centre and cafe.

members.name: Mount Sugarloaf Lookout
members.bio: A 412 m summit lookout at West Wallsend with views over Newcastle, Lake Macquarie, Cessnock and Maitland.

members.name: Lake Macquarie
members.bio: Australia's largest coastal lake, twice Sydney Harbour's size, with swim spots, lakeside parks and kayaking.

members.name: Caves Beach
members.bio: Surf beach famed for sea caves at low tide, ranked ninth in Tourism Australia's 2025 best beaches list.

members.name: Catherine Hill Bay
members.bio: A State Heritage-listed village, the oldest in Lake Macquarie, with a patrolled beach and wooden pier.

members.name: Redhead Beach
members.bio: A patrolled surf beach, first of Lake Macquarie's four, with a 24-hour off-leash dog section.

members.name: Blacksmiths Beach
members.bio: A patrolled family beach at the Swansea Channel breakwater, beside the shallow Grannies Pool.

members.name: Hunter Valley Gardens
members.bio: Ten themed gardens and 8 km of paths across 14 hectares on Broke Road in Pokolbin wine country.
members.hours: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM (last entry 4:00 PM); closed Christmas Day

members.name: Pokolbin
members.bio: Lower Hunter vineyards and cellar doors dating from the 1850s, spread across villages with no single centre.

members.name: Cessnock
members.bio: A vineyard service town with early 1900s buildings and a heritage walking-tour brochure.
members.photo_file: Vincent Street viewed from Maitland and Wollombi Road intersection in Cessnock.jpg

members.name: Morpeth
members.bio: A historic village on Maitland's outskirts with cafes and boutique shops, best visited Thursday to Sunday.
members.photo_file: Morpeth Bridge over the Hunter River (2).jpg

members.name: Maitland
members.bio: A historic Hunter city of heritage buildings, the Regional Art Gallery and Walka Water Works.

members.name: Wollombi
members.bio: A sandstone heritage village on the Great North Road with a courthouse museum, general store and tavern.

members.name: Watagans National Park
members.bio: A rainforest park with lookouts, the Gap Creek Falls walk and Aboriginal sites, an hour from Newcastle.

members.name: Stockton Beach
members.bio: A 32 km beach beside the largest moving coastal sand dune in the southern hemisphere, near Birubi Point.

members.name: Mount Tomaree
members.bio: A steep 2.2 km return climb to the 161 m summit of Tomaree Head, with WWII gun emplacements at the top.

members.name: Shoal Bay
members.bio: A sweep of calm white sand beside Tomaree Head, five minutes' drive from Nelson Bay.

members.name: Nelson Bay
members.bio: The Port Stephens hub where whale and dolphin cruises leave from the marina, with shore dives nearby.

members.name: Fingal Bay
members.bio: A white-sand patrolled surf beach under Fingal Head, with a whale-watching platform at Barry Park.

members.name: Anna Bay
members.bio: A surf village and gateway to the Stockton Bight dunes at Birubi Beach, with sandboarding and 4WD tours.

members.name: One Mile Beach
members.bio: A one-mile white-sand surf beach, patrolled in summer, with a kiosk and picnic reserve behind the dunes.
members.photo_file: One Mile Beach, Port Stephens, NSW, Australia (175371473).jpg

members.name: Point Stephens Lighthouse
members.bio: An 1862 lighthouse on Fingal Island with a unique swept tower base, visited by guided boat tour.
members.hours: Guided boat tours only; contact the operator for dates

members.name: Gan Gan Lookout
members.bio: A 160 m lookout on Gan Gan Hill with 360-degree views over the peninsula, reached by road without a hike.

members.name: Fly Point
members.bio: An aquatic reserve for snorkelling and shore diving, with sponge gardens and the odd seahorse metres off.

members.name: Australian Reptile Park
members.bio: A Somersby wildlife park with crocodiles, snakes, wombats and Tasmanian devils, plus daily crocodile shows.
members.photo_file: Entry to the Australian Reptile Park (78874325).jpg

members.name: Terrigal Beach
members.bio: A golden surf beach with a family rock pool at the southern end and an esplanade of cafes and restaurants.
members.photo_file: Terrigal Beach view from boardwalk - Australia Day.jpg

members.name: Bouddi National Park
members.bio: Cliffs, rainforest and beaches near Killcare, with a coastal walk and an early marine protected area.

members.name: Maitland Bay
members.bio: A secluded bay below a steep 2 km return track, where the 1898 PS Maitland wreck shows at low tide.
members.photo_file: Maitland Bay Trail, Bouddi National Park (16008319861).jpg

members.name: Bouddi Coastal Walk
members.bio: An 8 km walk from Putty Beach to MacMasters Beach with boardwalks, a whale-watching lookout and wildflowers.

members.name: Brisbane Water National Park
members.bio: Sandstone bushland with wildflowers, ancient Aboriginal rock engravings and walking and cycling trails.

members.name: Pearl Beach
members.bio: A beach village on the edge of the bush where the Patonga walk ends, with picnic spots and small cafes.

members.name: Patonga
members.bio: A fishing and holiday village on Brisk Bay near the Hawkesbury's mouth, with fish and chips by the beach.

members.name: Umina Beach
members.bio: A family beach on the Woy Woy peninsula with calm shallow water, a kiosk, picnic tables and lifeguards.

members.name: Pelican Feeding
members.bio: A daily 3:30 pm pelican feed on Pelican Plaza in The Entrance, the self-styled Pelican Capital of Australia.

members.name: The Skillion
members.bio: A headland lookout an easy walk from Terrigal Beach, with cliff and coast views and whales May to November.

members.name: Somersby Falls
members.bio: An 800 m return rainforest walk to a three-tier waterfall, with free barbecues and picnic tables.
members.hours: 7:00 AM – 8:00 PM daylight saving; 7:00 AM – 6:00 PM otherwise

members.name: Bulgandry Art Site
members.bio: Aboriginal rock engravings near Kariong, including a headdressed man, wallabies, fish and a canoe.

members.name: Wamberal Beach
members.bio: A long surf beach running north from Terrigal, considered one of the best on the NSW east coast.

members.name: Forresters Beach
members.bio: A surf beach between Terrigal and Bateau Bay, known for its clear water and reef breaks.

members.name: Putty Beach
members.bio: A surf beach and campground in Bouddi National Park, where the Bouddi Coastal Walk begins.

members.name: Little Beach
members.bio: A small beach with a walk-in campground, 3.5 km along the coastal walk from Maitland Bay.

members.name: Tallow Beach
members.bio: A remote beach reached by a steep 1.2 km management trail, with a walk-in campground near Killcare.

members.name: Wyrrabalong National Park
members.bio: A two-part coastal park holding the Central Coast's last coastal rainforest, with beaches and whale watching.

members.name: Patonga to Pearl Beach Walking Track
members.bio: A 3 km one-way bush walk between two beaches, passing Warrah lookout and sandstone caves.

members.name: Woy Woy
members.bio: A Brisbane Water town with waterfront seafood at Fishermen's Wharf and a one-hour scenic ferry round trip.

members.name: Great North Road
members.bio: A convict-built World Heritage road, walked as a 9 km loop past a quarry and stone buttresses.

members.name: Wisemans Ferry
members.bio: A Hawkesbury village with a free cable ferry crossing in use since 1829, and gateway to Dharug National Park.

members.name: Mount Gower
members.bio: Lord Howe's 875 m summit, reached only with a licensed guide on an eight-hour trek with rope-assisted climbs.
members.hours: Guided tours only; book ahead (about 8 hours return)
members.photo_file: Mount Gower, Lord Howe Island, NSW, Australia.jpg

members.name: Ned's Beach
members.bio: A calm north-east beach where you wade in to hand-feed fish and snorkel over a fringing coral reef.

members.name: Malabar Hill
members.bio: A two-hour return climb from Ned's Beach to cliff views and courting red-tailed tropicbirds, September to May.

members.name: Old Settlement Beach
members.bio: Weather-sculpted sandstone rocks dot the south end of this beach, where turtles are often seen close to shore.

members.name: Blinky Beach
members.bio: An unspoilt west-coast beach for surfing and swimming, reached on foot from Transit Hill or Lagoon Road.

members.name: North Bay
members.bio: A secluded north beach reached only on foot or by boat, with snorkelling over the wreck of the Favourite.
members.hours: Open 24 hours (Mt Eliza track closed 1 September to 1 March)
members.photo_file: Lord Howe Island from Mount Eliza.JPG

members.name: Intermediate Hill
members.bio: A steep 1 km climb to a 250 m summit platform with views across the island to Ball's Pyramid.

members.name: Transit Hill
members.bio: An easy 1.2 km walk from the Administration Office to a summit lookout with a 360-degree view.

members.name: Muttonbird Point
members.bio: A lookout platform on a short side track off the coastal walk, with open views out over the sea.

members.name: Goat House Cave
members.bio: A difficult 2.1 km climb up Smoking Tree Ridge to a cave, steep and narrow with rope-assisted sections.

members.name: Lord Howe Island Museum
members.bio: Island museum with history from 1788, World Heritage displays and a giant horned turtle skeleton.

members.name: Lagoon Beach
members.bio: A calm lagoon shore on the island's east side, lined with banyans and pandanus.
